written.myAnswer: The three types of RNA are mRNA, tRNA, and rRNA. mRNA carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes; tRNA brings specific amino acids to ribosomes during protein synthesis; rRNA forms part of the ribosomes and helps in protein synthesis.
DNA stores hereditary information in its nucleotide sequence. This information determines the amino acid sequence of proteins and is passed from one generation to the next.

DNA consists of two nucleotide strands coiled around each other to form a double helix. Bases on opposite strands pair by hydrogen bonds: adenine with thymine through two hydrogen bonds, and cytosine with guanine through three.

DNA’s nucleotide sequence contains the information for making proteins. This information is transcribed into mRNA, which carries it to a ribosome. There, tRNA brings amino acids in the order specified by the message, and they join to form a polypeptide that becomes a protein.
